_comment: Deterministic tier cases (issue #5, docs/pre_build_checklist.md §6). Provenance: constructed. Money values are PreciseNumber-style attoTIG decimal strings (accounting.md §3), computed with integer math only. J[k] and X are fixture policy inventions, NOT settled protocol constants (mining_system.md §11 leaves their numerical values open). Round aggregates U/V follow the minimal state model in architecture.md §7.6 (one aggregate row per member/tier membership/round). Expected values are recorded independently of any implementation; each names the rule that derives it.

conventions.money_unit: attoTIG decimal string (1 TIG = 10^18 attoTIG), accounting.md §3

fixture_policy.note: Numerical values for J[k] and X are intentionally left open in mining_system.md §11; these are fixture inventions carried as versioned policy inputs.

cases.name: paid_join_activates_tier
cases.description: Joining tier 2 debits J[2] from finalized unencumbered security-deposit value; tier activation and the balanced fee journal batch commit together.
cases.action_or_event: Member authorizes the tier-2 joining fee from finalized security-deposit value; the debit finalizes.

expected.derivation: 10 - 5 = 5 TIG remaining deposit; activation and the fee batch are one commit; the fee is non-refundable.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.3 (fee taken only from finalized, unencumbered security-deposit value; activation and the balanced fee journal batch commit together; tier removal creates no refund); mining_system.md §6.1 (joining tier k costs the versioned, non-refundable fee J[k])

cases.name: unfinalized_fee_debit_never_activates
cases.description: A failed, ambiguous, or unfinalized fee debit never activates the tier.
cases.action_or_event: Member attempts to join tier 1 but the fee debit does not finalize.

expected.derivation: No finalized fee, no activation; the member remains at tier NONE with zero concurrency.

cases.rule: accounting.md §11.3 (a failed, ambiguous, or unfinalized fee debit never activates the tier)

cases.name: k_unverified_enforcement_at_limit
cases.description: Tier k permits at most k concurrent unverified benchmarks; the admission check is member_unverified < tier_number inside the serialized precommit-admission lease.
cases.action_or_event: Controller recounts authoritative unverified workflows and evaluates admission for a third precommit intent.

expected.admission_if_member_unverified_were_1: allowed (1 < 2, given the collateral and global gates pass)
expected.derivation: Tier 2 caps concurrent unverified benchmarks at 2; the strict less-than check fails at the limit.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.1 (tier k permits at most k concurrent unverified benchmarks) and §10 invariant 22; architecture.md §7.6 (in the same transaction the Controller recounts authoritative unverified workflows and checks member_unverified < tier_number)

cases.name: unverified_span_survives_package_acceptance
cases.description: Durable package acceptance releases the compute slot but the benchmark stays unverified for tier concurrency until TIG verifies it or records a terminal outcome.

benchmark.state: package durably accepted, benchmark commitment submitted, not yet TIG-verified, not terminal

cases.action_or_event: Member offers the freed slot and the Controller evaluates admission for a new precommit intent.

expected.derivation: A benchmark is unverified from creation of its pool precommit intent until TIG records it verified or terminal stopped/expired/failed. Slot release at durable acceptance does not end the unverified interval, so the tier-1 member has no free unverified position.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.1 (a benchmark is unverified from creation of its pool precommit intent until TIG records it as verified or terminal; an accepted package releases its compute slot, but the benchmark remains unverified for tier concurrency) and §10 invariant 9

cases.name: rejoin_outstanding_unverified_counts_against_new_tier
cases.description: A removed member with still-unverified benchmarks buys a tier again; those benchmarks immediately count against the newly purchased tier.
cases.action_or_event: Member pays J[2] and rejoins at tier 2, then requests new work.

expected.derivation: Repurchase is allowed immediately (no cooldown, no admission queue) but does not reset protocol state: both pre-removal unverified benchmarks count against the new tier-2 allowance, so no new precommit is admitted until one resolves.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.1 (a removed member may buy a tier again immediately; an immediate repurchase does not reset protocol state — every still-unverified benchmark continues to count against the newly purchased tier) and §10 invariant 22 (including benchmarks created before the current tier purchase)

cases.name: rejoin_no_cooldown_no_refund_liabilities_persist
cases.description: Removal then immediate repurchase: the old fee is not refunded, the new fee is charged in a new idempotent batch, and reservations/fines/method exposure survive both removal and rejoin.
cases.action_or_event: Member immediately pays J[2] again and rejoins.

new_fee_batch.batch_id: fee_batch_fake_002 (new idempotent batch, new membership period)

expected.derivation: No cooldown or admission queue; no refund; every purchase creates a new idempotent fee batch and membership period; removal and rejoin change neither the open reservation nor the frozen charge.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (the member can immediately purchase any allowed tier by paying J[k] again; there is no cooldown; rejoining does not clear open benchmarks, round evidence, security reservations, fines, or method penalties) and §10 invariant 24; accounting.md §11.3 (every purchase has a new idempotent fee batch and membership period)

cases.name: dormancy_has_no_tier_consequence
cases.description: A member with no unverified and no verified/active benchmarks all round contributes zero to both aggregates and is not removed.
cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated.

expected.check: U > V is 0 > 0 = false; f > k is 0 > 3 = false
expected.derivation: Dormancy adds zero to both aggregates, so neither removal rule fires. The repeated non-refundable joining fee, not a dormancy penalty, is the deterrent against cycling dormant identities.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (a member with no current unverified or verified/active benchmarks contributes zero to both aggregates; dormancy by itself has no tier consequence)

cases.name: round_U_greater_than_V_removes_tier
cases.description: At round close, unverified exposure exceeding verified exposure removes the tier membership (v0 slow-work/clogging rule).
cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated.

expected.derivation: The sums are comparable directly because both aggregates share the same sample_count. Removal follows from U > V alone; no X is charged because f = 0.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (if unverified_exposure[m, round] > verified_exposure[m, round]: remove tier membership; the averages can be compared by comparing their sums because they have the same sample count; removal means tier = NONE, concurrency zero, and no new precommits)

cases.name: round_U_equal_V_retains_tier
cases.description: The removal rule is a strict inequality: equal exposure sums do not remove the tier.
cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated.

expected.derivation: The documented condition is strictly greater-than; equality retains the membership.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (removal fires only when unverified_exposure > verified_exposure)

cases.name: per_failure_charge_X_below_boundary
cases.description: Each chargeable failed benchmark charges X from reserved security collateral; with f <= k the tier is retained.
cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated.

expected.charge_mechanism: freeze then charge exactly X per failure from that benchmark's reservation, under the assignment's policy version
expected.check: f > k is 2 > 3 = false; U > V is 10 > 30 = false
expected.derivation: f * X = 2 * 2 TIG = 4 TIG. Each failure consumes its own benchmark's reservation; one benchmark never consumes another benchmark's reserve. Tier retained because both removal conditions are false.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (each failure charges the versioned amount X from reserved security collateral); accounting.md §11.6 (for every chargeable tier failure, freeze and then charge exactly X under the assignment's policy version; multiple failing benchmarks use their own reservations and batches)

cases.name: f_greater_than_k_removal_boundary
cases.description: The removal boundary is strict: f = k charges f*X and retains the tier; f = k + 1 charges f*X and additionally removes the tier at round close.

input_state.round_aggregate_note: U <= V in both sub-cases so only the f rule is in play

cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated for each sub-case.

over_boundary.removal_timing: at round close, in addition to the f * X charge

expected.derivation: 2 * 2 TIG = 4 TIG (retained); 3 * 2 TIG = 6 TIG plus removal. Removal is additional to, not instead of, the per-failure charges.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (if f > k, the member's tier membership is removed at round close in addition to the f * X charge); accounting.md §11.6 (for tier k, if the round's chargeable failure count f > k, remove the tier at round close after recording the ordinary f * X charges)

cases.name: non_chargeable_outcomes_do_not_increment_f
cases.description: POOL, TIG, compatibility, and UNRESOLVED outcomes, and TIG-verified work that merely earns no qualifiers, charge zero and never increment f.

round_outcomes.outcome: upload failed due to confirmed pool infrastructure failure
TIG infrastructure failed independently of the member
TIG-verified, active bundles earned no qualifiers

cases.action_or_event: Round r834 closes and the tier decision is evaluated.

expected.fraud_labels: none — valid low-quality or non-qualifying work is never mislabeled as fraud
expected.derivation: None of the four outcomes is a chargeable member failure, so f stays 0 and no X is frozen or charged. bench_b64 is recorded as an unresolved operational outcome rather than an automatic penalty.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (pool, TIG, compatibility, or unresolved incidents are neither tier failures nor chargeable member failures; ordinary non-qualifying work that TIG does verify is not a tier failure) and §10 invariant 18; accounting.md §11.6 (POOL, TIG, compatibility, and UNRESOLVED outcomes charge zero and do not increment f; for TIG-verified work that merely earns no qualifiers, charge zero)

cases.name: zero_quality_bundles_chargeable_not_fraud
cases.description: A complete, valid benchmark with zero bundles meeting TIG's minimum verification quality is a chargeable tier failure (capacity/economic policy) without being labeled fraud.

benchmark.state: complete, structurally valid, no bundle meets TIG's minimum verification quality

cases.action_or_event: The outcome is attributed and recorded for the round.

expected.derivation: f increments to 1 and exactly X = 2 TIG is frozen then charged; the record describes a capacity/economic failure, not fraud.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (a benchmark with no bundles meeting TIG's minimum verification quality counts as a chargeable failure for this tier policy even though it is not described as fraud); accounting.md §11.6 (for zero bundles meeting TIG's minimum verification quality, charge X under the tier policy without describing the outcome as fraud)

cases.name: removal_cancels_offers_not_precommit_intents
cases.description: Tier removal cancels queued offers and unconfirmed ready checks in one transaction, but a precommit intent created before removal remains an outstanding member-owned benchmark.
cases.action_or_event: Tier membership is removed at round close.

expected.cancellation_atomicity: closing the membership and cancelling still-queued/ready-check offers is one transaction

surviving.bench_b67: remains an outstanding member-owned benchmark following its normal terminal path, with its financial exposure still attached to member_m23

expected.post_removal_offers: after rejoining, the member sends fresh availability offers
expected.derivation: Offers and ready checks carry no protocol commitment and are cancelled; the precommit intent does carry one and survives.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (removal cancels queued offers and unconfirmed ready checks because they contain no protocol commitment; a precommit intent already created before removal remains an outstanding member-owned benchmark); architecture.md §7.6 (closing a tier membership and cancelling its still-queued/ready-check offers is one transaction; offers that already own a precommit intent are not cancelled)

cases.name: removal_at_round_close_rejoin_gets_fresh_aggregates
cases.description: Because evaluation occurs at round close, a removed member who rejoins normally starts the new membership in the new round with a new aggregate row and fresh U/V/f, while pre-removal round evidence is retained.
cases.action_or_event: Member is removed at round r834 close, pays J[1] and rejoins in round r835.

expected.r834_evidence: retained unchanged; rejoining does not clear round evidence
expected.derivation: One aggregate row exists per member/tier membership/round, so the new membership in the new round starts a new row at zero. The r834 row and its removal decision remain the audit record.

cases.rule: mining_system.md §8 (because evaluation occurs at round close, a removed member normally begins a newly purchased membership in the new round with new round aggregates; rejoining does not clear round evidence); architecture.md §7.6 (one aggregate row per member/tier membership/round containing sample count, unverified benchmark-blocks, verified benchmark-blocks, chargeable failure count, and the resulting tier decision)
